tool.name: UMI isolation
tool.description: Use a python script to cluster all umis and output a tabular file, a blast file and a zip file.
tool.command:
set -euo pipefail &&
WORK_DIR="$(mktemp -d umi_isolation_work.XXXXXX)" CLUSTER_DIR="$(mktemp -d umi_isolation_cluster.XXXXXX)"
python3 $__tool_directory__/umi-isolation.py -o $output_tabular -z "${WORK_DIR}/" -c "${CLUSTER_DIR}/" -q $output_fasta -p $search_approach_options.process -f $input_files.input.single -l $additional_options.umi_length -s $search_method_options.search_method -a $additional_options.forward -b $additional_options.reverse -d $additional_options.identity_score -u $additional_options.abundance_score #if $input_files.input.single == "fastq" -i $input_files.input.single_fastq #elif $input_files.input.single == "fasta" -i $input_files.input.single_fasta #end if &&
find "${WORK_DIR}/" -name "derep*" -delete && find "${WORK_DIR}/" -name "sorted*" -delete && find "${WORK_DIR}/" -name "UMI#*" -print | zip -jqr $output_zip -@ && rm -rf "${WORK_DIR}" "${CLUSTER_DIR}"

param.name: single
param.label: Input type
param.help: Select the type of input data you are providing

param.name: process
param.label: Primer, scaffold(adapter) or first position?
param.help: The tool will use the following format: [Forward_Scaffold(Adapter)]-[Forward_UMI]-[Forward_Primer]--READ--[Reverse_Primer]-[Reverse_UMI]-[Reverse_Scaffold(Adapter)]

param.name: search_method
param.label: Search umis at 5'-end [umi5], 3'-end [umi3] or at 5'-end and 3'-end [umidouble]
param.help: Searching with umi5 instructs the tool to only search for umis at the start of every read, searching with umi3 instructs the tool to only search for umis at the end of every read, while umidouble will instruct the tool to collect umis on both the start and end of every read

param.name: umi_length
param.label: The length of the umi sequences (INTEGER)
param.help: Enter a integer that represents the length of a single umi

param.name: abundance_score
param.label: The minimum abundance
param.help: Enter the minimum abundance with which a read needs to be present in order to not be discarded

param.name: identity_score
param.label: The identity percentage
param.help: The identity percentage with which vsearch will cluster isolated reads within a single umi fasta file

tool.help:
.. class:: infomark This tool uses the output from Primer3 generic/check_primers or Primer3-py, look there in order to find out how to generate output to use as input for this tool.
Use a python script to accumulate all umis and output a tabular file, a blast file and a zip file.
The tabular file will contain all unique umi nucleotides, a count of the number of reads that are associated with that umi and a unique identifier for every umi.
The blast file can be used to identify all umi clusters.
The zip file will contain fasta files for every unique umi and contain reads associated with that umi, this zip file is created before vsearch is used for a final check.
.. class:: warningmark Every read in a fasta file should have a header starting with >. Every read in a fastq file should have a header starting with @. Every read in a fasta/fastq file should be on one line. For instance they can not be "human readable" and have a "\\n" after every 80 characters.
